question: The board sets effort to the maximum on an easy rename. What happens to the answer, the cost and the wait?

options.why: Tempting. It is easy to count only what the user reads, but the thinking is billed too.

options.text: The thinking tokens and the answer tokens together.

question: A reply has some thinking and then an answer. Which tokens are billed as output?

options.text: The answer improves, and the cost rises a little.
options.why: Tempting. On easy work the answer often does not change, so the extra cost buys nothing.

options.text: The answer often stays the same, and the cost and the wait rise a lot.
options.why: Right. Thinking is output, so the cost and the wait grow with it.

options.text: The answer stays the same, and the cost falls.
options.why: Wrong. More thinking means more output, so the cost goes up.

question: On easy work, effort goes from low to the maximum. What changes?

options.text: Trims it, to save tokens before the next call.
options.why: Tempting. Trimming saves tokens, but the block must come back unchanged.

options.text: Passes it back complete and unmodified, with the tool call it belongs to.
options.why: Right. The docs say thinking blocks must be passed back complete and unmodified alongside the tool_use block.

options.text: Removes it, because it is not part of the answer.
options.why: Wrong. Removing it changes what the model sees on the next call.

question: During a tool loop, the reply carries a thinking block next to a tool call. What does the harness do with it?

options.text: The highest level, to be safe, since it can only help.
options.why: Tempting. It can add cost and wait without a better answer on easy work.

options.text: A low level, checked by the tests, because cost per completed task falls when the tasks still finish.
options.why: Right. The choice is measured by cost per completed task, and it holds only if the tasks finish at the same rate.

options.text: No level, because thinking is free.
options.why: Wrong. The docs say thinking is billed as output.
